title: Post-Trade & Custody
intro: This level covers clearing, settlement and custody, including fails and CSDR penalties, segregation and depositary protection, transfers, and securities lending and repo collateral. It also covers the processing of mandatory corporate actions with correct dates and entitlements, and bond price, yield, duration and convexity.

modules.title: Clearing & CCPs
modules.hook: The role of central counterparties, novation, clearing members, initial and variation margin, default funds, and intraday margin calls.

units.title: Why clearing exists: counterparty risk and netting
objectives: Learner can explain why a bilateral trade carries counterparty risk between trade date and settlement date
Learner can compute bilateral net obligations from a list of trades
Learner can distinguish clearing from settlement
units.worked_example: Bank A buys 10,000 shares at EUR 20 from B and sells 6,000 at EUR 20.40 to B the same day; bilateral netting reduces two gross deliveries to a single net 4,000-share delivery and a net cash amount.

units.worked_example: A client transfers in 1,000 shares: 400 bought on 12 Mar 2019 at EUR 18.00 and 600 on 30 Jun 2021 at EUR 22.50. units.title: Cash dividends: gross, tax, net, currency
objectives: Learner can compute gross and net dividend entitlement from a position and a rate
Learner can apply withholding tax at source and explain reclaim-at-source concepts
Learner can describe DRIP vs cash dividend and dividend currency (pay-in-EUR vs currency option) at a basic level
key_concepts: dividend per share, gross vs net
dividend on settled vs contractual position
units.worked_example: 10,000 shares x EUR 1.20 = EUR 12,000 gross; with 26% withholding the client receives EUR 8,880 and the custodian posts the tax separately.

exercises.task: Compute net dividend after withholding
Compute entitlement on a position changed by an unsettled trade
Fill a dividend payment run for 6 clients (gross, tax, net)
Choose the correct event for a described payment
Spot the arithmetic error in a dividend advice

units.title: Stock dividends and bonus issues
objectives: Learner can compute entitlement for a stock dividend or bonus issue with fractions
Learner can explain how a bonus issue differs from a split
Learner can explain the effect on price and holdings
key_concepts: fractional entitlements and cash in lieu
units.worked_example: 1 new share per 10 held: 1,234 shares entitle to 123 new shares and 0.4 fraction, settled as cash in lieu; the price drops by about 1/11 on the ex-date.

exercises.task: Compute new shares and cash in lieu
Compute theoretical ex-price after a bonus
Decide whether an event changes company value
Update a position table after a bonus issue

units.title: Splits and reverse splits
objectives: Learner can compute post-split holdings and prices
Learner can handle fractions in reverse splits
Learner can describe impacts on orders, options and static data
units.worked_example: A 4-for-1 split turns 500 shares at EUR 200 into 2,000 at EUR 50; in a 1-for-10 reverse split, 1,234 shares become 123 new shares plus a 0.4 fraction settled in cash.

exercises.task: Compute post-split holdings and price
Compute fractions and cash payment for a reverse split
Pick the correct adjustment for a resting limit order
Spot the error in a split notice

units.title: Coupons and interest payments
objectives: Learner can compute coupon payments with day-count conventions
Learner can apply business-day conventions to payment dates
Learner can distinguish fixed, floating and zero-coupon cases
units.worked_example: EUR 1,000,000 nominal at 3.5% annual: coupon EUR 35,000; if the payment date falls on a Saturday it is paid the next business day (unadjusted) without extra interest.

exercises.task: Compute a coupon payment
Place coupon dates around a weekend/holiday
Compute an FRN coupon from fixing and margin
Classify the payment type
Spot the error in a coupon notice

units.title: Redemptions: maturity, calls, drawings, pool factors
objectives: Learner can compute redemption proceeds for full and partial redemptions
Learner can apply pool factors to nominal positions
Learner can distinguish call, drawing and put (voluntary, see O8)
units.worked_example: A holder of EUR 1,000,000 original face sees the factor drop from 0.80 to 0.65: EUR 150,000 is repaid and the remaining nominal is EUR 650,000.

exercises.task: Compute proceeds of a partial redemption from a factor change
Compute redemption with premium and accrued interest
Match terms to events (call, drawing, factor)
Sort redemption events into mandatory vs holder's option
Update a position after a drawing

units.title: Mandatory reorganisations: mergers, exchanges, spin-offs
objectives: Learner can compute entitlements for a mandatory merger or exchange with fractions
Learner can explain demerger/spin-off treatment and squeeze-outs
Learner can describe the position and static-data changes
units.worked_example: A 3-for-2 share exchange turns 1,001 old shares into 1,501.5 new shares: 1,501 delivered and 0.5 settled in cash.

exercises.task: Compute new shares and cash for an exchange
Choose the right event type
Update positions and ISINs after a merger
Spot the error in a merger notice

units.title: Identifier, name and other static-data changes
objectives: Learner can handle ISIN, name and other static-data changes without economic impact
Learner can map old to new identifiers in positions and tax lots
Learner can list downstream systems affected by an identifier change
units.worked_example: A company changes name and ISIN: the position quantity stays 10,000, the old ISIN is closed and the new opened with the same cost basis.

exercises.task: Match changes to affected data fields
Decide whether the event is economic or static
Re-key a position and lot table to the new ISIN
Order the steps for a static-data event

units.title: Messaging and reconciliation: MT564-568 and seev
objectives: Learner can read an MT564/seev.031 notification
Learner can map MT564/565/566/567/568 to their ISO 20022 equivalents
Learner can reconcile an event payment and handle breaks
key_concepts: field qualifiers (CAEV, CAMV, XDTE, RDTE, PAYD)
units.worked_example: An MT564 shows CAEV//DVCA, CAMV//MAND, XDTE 11 June, RDTE 12 June, PAYD 19 June and a gross rate of EUR 1.20; the desk computes expected cash and matches it with the MT566 confirmation.

exercises.task: Match MT messages to their ISO 20022 seev equivalents
Read the event type and key dates from a notification extract
Spot the error in an MT564 extract
Reconcile the expected cash with the received amount
Order the CA message flow

minigame.name: CA Election Desk
minigame.variant: Mandatory-events edition: process a stream of mandatory events on the right dates, compute entitlements and match payments; elections added in O8.

modules.unit_test: Event classification and lifecycle, key-date logic, cash and share entitlements for every mandatory event type, and notification reading.
modules.jurisdiction_notes: EU first (CAJWG standards, T2S/CSD announcements, ISO 20022 seev); US sidebar (DTC announcements, record-date practice, T+1 ex-date alignment); UK/CH/SG/HK differences only noted (e.g. UK ex-coupon periods).

modules.title: Fixed income maths I
modules.hook: Bond price from yield, yield to maturity, duration, modified duration and convexity, and their use in estimating the price effect of a yield change.

units.title: Price as present value; the price-yield relationship
objectives: Learner can price a fixed-coupon bond by discounting cash flows
Learner can explain why price and yield move inversely and why the curve is convex
Learner can compare coupon, yield and price (par, discount, premium)
units.worked_example: A 5-year 4% annual bond priced at a 3% yield: 4 x 4.5797 + 100 x 0.86261 = EUR 104.58 per 100.

exercises.task: Price a bond from coupon, maturity and yield
Complete a PV table of cash flows
Predict price direction for a yield move
Classify a bond as par, premium or discount

units.title: Yield measures and conventions
objectives: Learner can compute current yield and yield to maturity approximations
Learner can solve YTM numerically by bracketing
Learner can distinguish annual, semi-annual and street conventions
key_concepts: dirty vs clean in yield calculations
units.worked_example: A 5-year 4% bond priced at 104.58 has YTM 3% (bracket between 2.5% and 3.5% and interpolate); current yield is 4/104.58 = 3.82%.

exercises.task: Compute current yield
Estimate YTM by bracketing
Pick the convention behind a quoted yield
Match yield measures to what they ignore

units.title: Duration: Macaulay and modified
objectives: Learner can compute Macaulay duration of a simple bond
Learner can derive modified duration and link it to the derivative of price w.r.t. yield
Learner can estimate price change from duration
units.worked_example: A 5-year 4% bond at 3% has Macaulay duration about 4.6 years, modified duration about 4.5; a +50 bp yield move implies roughly -2.2% price.

exercises.task: Compute Macaulay duration from weights
Estimate price change from modified duration
Explain what happens to duration when coupon rises
Complete the link between duration and the derivative

units.title: DV01, portfolio duration and hedging
objectives: Learner can compute DV01 / PVBP
Learner can compute portfolio duration as a weighted average
Learner can size a simple duration hedge
units.worked_example: A EUR 10m position with modified duration 4.5 has DV01 about EUR 4,500 per bp.

exercises.task: Compute DV01 from market value and duration
Compute portfolio duration
Size a hedge to neutralise DV01
Identify the risk duration does not capture

units.title: Convexity and second-order price change
objectives: Learner can compute convexity for a simple bond
Learner can apply the Taylor estimate with duration and convexity
Learner can explain negative convexity in callables
units.worked_example: With duration 4.5 and convexity 25, a +100 bp move: -4.5% + 0.5 x 25 x 0.0001 = -4.4%, i.e. convexity adds back about 0.125 percentage points.

exercises.task: Compute price change with duration + convexity
Compute error vs exact repricing
Choose the instrument with negative convexity
Complete the Taylor expansion terms
Optional: explain convexity to a client in writing

modules.unit_test: Bond pricing by PV, yield measures, duration, DV01 and convexity arithmetic.
modules.jurisdiction_notes: EU conventions (ICMA) first; US street conventions as a sidebar; UK/CH/SG/HK noted only where quoting differs.

checkpoint: Boss quiz (35-45 min, ~30 questions) mixing O2-O7 and F3: netting and margin arithmetic, settlement-date and penalty calculations, segregation and depositary scenarios, SFT collateral numbers, entitlement computations for each mandatory event type, and a duration/convexity estimate. Mix of numeric, timeline, spot-the-error and match items, with 20-30% spaced-review items from L1-L3.
